chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ahmad ibn Hilal, from Isa ibn Abdullah al-Hashimi, from his father, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:
The place of the Ka'ba was a mound of white earth, shining like the light of the sun and the moon, until the two sons of Adam — one of the two — killed his companion, and it turned black.

When Adam descended, Allah raised the earth, all of it, for him until he saw it, then said: 'This is for you, all of it.' He said: 'O Lord! What is this white, radiant land?' He said: 'It is in My land, and I have made it incumbent upon you to circumambulate it seven hundred times every day.'

key_terms.رَبْوَة: A mound or elevated piece of ground
key_terms.سَبْعَمِائَةِ طَوَافٍ: Seven hundred circumambulations — a heavenly/primordial measure before the earthly Hajj was prescribed
key_terms.طَوَافٍ: Circumambulation — the ritual of walking around the Ka'ba, central to Hajj and Umra
key_terms.فَاسْوَدَّتْ: It turned black — the earth's radiance was extinguished by the first act of murder
key_terms.مَوْضِعُ الْكَعْبَةِ: The place/site of the Ka'ba — the sacred ground where the Ka'ba now stands

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about the original state of the Ka'ba's location before creation?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) describes the primordial status of the Ka'ba's site: before Cain killed Abel, it shone with brilliant white light like the sun and moon, but turned black due to the first murder. When Adam descended to earth, God showed him the entire world and, in response to Adam's wonder at the white luminous spot, revealed it as a sacred site within His earth and commanded Adam to perform 700 circumambulations around it daily — a cosmic precursor to the Hajj rite that would be formalized through Ibrahim (AS) millennia later.
